title: Entity registration

title: Contract Opportunities
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Contract opportunities are notices from federal contracting offices (pre-solicitation, solicitation, award and sole source notices); anyone may search without an account; a free login.gov account saves searches and follows changes

title: Basic requirements (federal contracting guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Steps to become a federal contractor: SAM.gov registration, the 12-character UEI, NAICS codes, SBA size standards, keeping compliant, and CMMC for DoD work

title: FAR Part 15: Contracting by Negotiation (FAC 2026-01, effective 13 March 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Best value tradeoff vs lowest price technically acceptable (15.101), avoiding LPTA for knowledge-based services (15.101-2(d)), oral presentations (15.102), evaluation factors and past performance (15.304), documenting strengths, weaknesses, deficiencies and risks and neutral past performance (15.305), discussions and final proposal revisions (15.306-15.307), debriefings (15.505-15.506)

title: FAR 2.101 Definitions (FAC 2026-01, effective 13 March 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. General micro-purchase threshold of $15,000 and simplified acquisition threshold of $350,000 as shown on 6 Nov 2026

title: Revolutionary FAR Overhaul
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The FAR is being rewritten in plain language with most non-statutory rules removed, started under the executive order 'Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement'; press releases dated August 2025 and June 2026 on the page. Status of each part was not readable from the page

title: Applicant registration
publisher: Grants.gov (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Organisations register with SAM.gov first (free, renewed yearly); allow up to 10 business days for SAM to become active; the E-Business Point of Contact sets up the organisation and assigns roles such as Authorized Organization Representative (AOR)

title: Grant eligibility
publisher: Grants.gov (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Eligible applicant types; most opportunities are for organisations; none provide personal financial assistance; each NOFO's eligibility section is the authority

title: Workspace overview
publisher: Grants.gov (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Workspace is the standard way to apply; teams fill forms in parallel online or offline; an AOR submits; external users such as consultants can be given form access by the Workspace Owner

title: Transforming Public Procurement
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Procurement Act 2023 came into force on 24 February 2025; the central digital platform is an enhanced Find a Tender plus a Supplier Information Service with one supplier account

title: The Procurement Act 2023: a short guide for suppliers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Free registration on the central digital platform, needed when you want to bid; information asked for; bid assessments for final tenders; 30-day payment terms across more contracts; competitive flexible procedure

title: New legislative requirements under the Procurement Act 2023
supports: Opened with WebFetch. From 1 April 2026, suppliers awarded notifiable below-threshold contracts (12,000 GBP central government including NHS; 30,000 GBP sub-central) must register and share a unique identifier; KPIs on contracts above 5m GBP with the three most material published yearly; payment compliance notices

title: The Procurement Act 2023: the competitive flexible procedure and negotiation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Stages are set out in the tender notice or documents; negotiation may happen at any stage if the documents allow it; suppliers should generally get the same chance to negotiate

title: Find a Tender: search
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Search published notices; sign in with GOV.UK One Login to register a buyer or supplier organisation, save searches and get email alerts

title: Contracts Finder
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Search contract opportunities by keyword, location and stage (early engagement, future opportunity, opportunity, awarded)

title: Small and Medium Business Hub
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Where to find UK public notices and framework opportunities; government aims to pay 90% of invoices in 5 days and all within 30; prompt payment expectations on bidders for major contracts

title: PPN 017: Improving transparency of AI use in procurement (17 February 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Suppliers may use AI to prepare bids; buyers may ask suppliers to disclose AI use (example questions are for information, not scored); risk of inaccurate or misleading AI text; extra checks such as clarification questions, presentations or site visits

title: PPN 026: The Social Value Model
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Applies to central government procurements commenced on or after 1 January 2027 worth 1m GBP or more; social value weighted at least 10% (1m to under 5m GBP) or 20% (5m GBP or more); outcomes on good jobs and skills; at least one social value KPI on contracts of 5m GBP or more

title: PPN 014: Cyber Essentials scheme
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Which central government contracts need Cyber Essentials or Cyber Essentials Plus (personal data of citizens or staff, ICT holding OFFICIAL data, government business information), proof before data passes, annual renewal, no blanket approach

title: Cyber Essentials: overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The five technical controls; Cyber Essentials Plus adds independent technical testing; IASME runs certification by self-assessment or a licensed certification body

title: Find a grant
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Beta service to search UK government grants, check eligibility and sign in to apply

title: Public tendering rules
supports: Opened with WebFetch. EU rules apply above thresholds; above-threshold tenders are published on TED; procedures (open, restricted, competitive with negotiation, competitive dialogue, innovation partnership); prior information notices 35 days to 12 months ahead; weighted award criteria; losing bidders are entitled to an explanation

title: Thresholds (public procurement)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. EU thresholds for 2026-2027: 140,000 EUR central government supplies and services; 216,000 EUR sub-central; 5,404,000 EUR works; 750,000 EUR social and other specific services; set by Delegated Regulations (EU) 2025/2150, 2025/2151, 2025/2152 and 2025/2487

title: European Single Procurement Document and eCertis
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The ESPD is a self-declaration that replaces certificates at bid stage; only the winner provides the documents; the Commission's own ESPD service closed on 2 May 2019, so national services are used

title: Funding and tenders
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Grants answer calls for proposals for projects that serve EU policy; tenders answer calls for tender when the Commission buys; the Funding and Tenders Portal and TED are where calls are found

title: The application process (EU funding)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Applications go through the Funding and Tenders Portal; find a call, find partners, register the organisation, submit electronically on time; late or incomplete proposals can be rejected; proposals that ignore the call documents can be ruled inadmissible

title: Award procedure and contract signature (EU funding)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Evaluation by Commission staff or independent specialists against the criteria in the call; order of eligibility and exclusion, selection, then award criteria; reserve lists; the grant agreement is the reference document

title: Color Team Reviews: who to invite and why
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated, no author shown). Blue, Black Hat, Pink, Red, Green, Gold and White Hat reviews: what each checks, when it happens and who should review

title: APMP: Association of Proposal Management Professionals
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Professional body for bid, proposal, capture and business development staff; certifications start at Foundation level, plus micro-certifications

title: RFP Response Trends and Benchmarks Report 2026
supports: Opened with WebFetch (summary page; full report gated). Seventh annual report, 1,500+ participants: average 166 RFPs submitted a year; management consulting 229; advertising lowest at 22 hours per RFP; 92% of software teams use AI in their RFP process. Vendor survey
